display.title: Episode 195: The Baal Shem Tov and 'Baruch Hashem' (Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan)
display.summary_short: A Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan show: holding on to the inspiration of Elul and Tishrei, the brachah on a mezuzah, a guest from Denver, and a new 'Baruch Hashem' song.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on Rosh Chodesh Cheshvan 5746, the first show after the Sukkos break. Uncle Yossi looks back over Elul and Tishrei: Hashem as a king in the field, the shofar moving Hashem from the throne of judgment to the throne of mercy, Tashlich, the Ten Days of Teshuvah, Yom Kippur, the joy of Sukkos and the dancing of Simchas Torah, and asks children to keep those memories alive all year. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, Mitzvah Time continues on the mezuzah: every room except the bathroom needs one, and the brachah 'likboa mezuzah' is said just before it is put up on the upper third of the right doorpost, ideally with the family there to answer amen. An eleven-year-old guest from Denver, visiting his grandparents in Crown Heights, leads the Shema and recites a Mishnah from Bava Kamma about damages. Story time tells how the Baal Shem Tov went to the marketplace to ask people how they were, just to hear them answer 'Baruch Hashem', and teaches a new song, 'Baruch Hashem, Baruch Hashem is what I always say'. The show ends with the Tishrei Mitzvah Mission card.
display.lesson: Say 'Baruch Hashem' as often as you can; every time you do, you bless Hashem and He blesses you.
